text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Government may favour a sale by private auction to privatise Thomson-CSF (Les Echos)
-- Dutch services group Vendex to buy 59.04 percent of temporary work agency BIS (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- Government may be ready to provide 12 billion francs in recapitalisation being sought by state bank Credit Lyonnais, with aim of privatising the bank in 1998 (Liberation)
LES ECHOS
-- Labour Minister Jacques Barrot to meet with unions and employers this week to launch talks on labour flexibility.
-- Insurer AGF sells subsidiary Banque du Phenix to Dutch banking group ABN Amro.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Renault carmaker seeks to improve productivity and react faster to adapt to demand and fend off competitors.

-- EU Commissioner for Agriculture Franz Fischler in an interview calls for a return of economic activity to rural areas, says EU help to agricultural sector should expand to benefit to all economic actors of rural areas.
L'AGEFI
-- Axa sells a 8.23 percent stake in retail store Galeries Lafayette for 289 million francs.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE

-- EU report to be published on January 13 shows the responsibility of EU authorities and British government in the mismanagement of BSE "mad cow" crisis, says they sought to protect the meat industry rather than public health.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Utility suppliers, salt producers, clothing industry benefit from the cold spell, but agriculture is hit by frost.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Turnaround in jet market triggers surge of orders for Airbus aircraft manufacturers consortium.
-- France and Germany face disappointing economic prospects for 1997 as unemployment surges and growth remains sluggish.
